hints: Look closely at the functional group in X, the $\text{-COO-}$ link tells you which homologous series it belongs to.
Split the ester into its two parts, the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{O-}$ side gives the alkyl name and the $\text{H-C=O}$ side gives the acid part.
Compare hydrogen bonding ability, remember only molecules with $\text{O-H}$ or $\text{N-H}$ can donate hydrogen bonds to themselves.
walkthrough:
**Spot the functional group**

Great start, let's look at what X actually is. The group $\text{-C(=O)-O-}$ in the middle is the ester link.

So X is an ester, not a carboxylic acid, aldehyde or alcohol.

**Name the ester correctly**

Esters are named as alkyl alkanoate. Think of it as alcohol part first, then acid part.

Alcohol part: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{O-}$ is 3 carbons, so propyl.
$$\text{HCOOH = methanoic acid, so HCOO- = methanoate}$$
Acid part: $\text{H-C(=O)-}$ comes from methanoic acid, so methanoate. Put together: propyl methanoate.

**Compare boiling points with butanoic acid**

Now for the physical property. Both X ($\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$) and butanoic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$) have the same molecular mass, so look at intermolecular forces.

Butanoic acid has $\text{O-H}$ and forms strong hydrogen bonds between its own molecules. The ester has no $\text{O-H}$, so it cannot hydrogen bond to itself, it only has weaker permanent dipole-dipole forces. Less energy is needed to separate ester molecules, so its boiling point is lower.

options.A: Incorrect on both parts. Methyl propanoate would be $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_3$, with the 3-carbon chain on the carbonyl side, which is reversed here. An ester also cannot have a higher boiling point than its isomeric carboxylic acid because it lacks hydrogen bond donation.
options.B: The boiling point comparison is right, but the name is wrong. Methyl propanoate puts the methyl on the alcohol side and propanoate on the acid side. Here the H is directly on the carbonyl carbon, so the acid part is only C1 (methanoate), not C3.
options.C: The name propyl methanoate is correct, but the boiling point trend is reversed. Students sometimes think the ester is more polar or larger, but butanoic acid forms intermolecular hydrogen bonds while the ester cannot, so the acid has the higher boiling point.
options.D: Correct on both counts. X is $\text{HCOOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, propyl methanoate. As an ester with no $\text{O-H}$ group it cannot hydrogen bond to itself, so its boiling point is lower than that of butanoic acid which has strong hydrogen bonding.
